selected_problem: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. Fresh-main inspection found that `WorkspaceService.contextBundle` applies its `maxFiles` slice before credential, text-type, symlink, existence and size admission filters. Rejected paths therefore consume the file-count budget. A recovery request or semantic seed with 32 rejected paths before a valid source file can return an empty bundle even though readable in-policy repository context is available later in the same request, prematurely starving native synthesis of code reality.

execution.route_basis: The new canonical main still exposes the native-complex-synthesis truth boundary. This is a single high-centrality context-acquisition defect with direct pre/post reproduction and no need to prescribe a new cognition architecture, so source-contract replay routes to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced mode rotation.

asset_reuse: Reused the existing credential-path, text-extension, ancestor/symlink, workspace path and byte-budget admission policies inside `WorkspaceService.contextBundle`.
No new selector, provider, model, product form or cognition architecture was introduced.
changes: `contextBundle` now iterates the deduplicated request set and stops only after `maxFiles` accepted files have been collected.
Rejected or unreadable paths no longer consume the accepted-file budget; byte limits and all existing safety filters remain unchanged.
Input order and deterministic first-accepted semantics are preserved.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED against fresh main: focused regression 0/1 PASS. Thirty-two nested credential-like paths consumed the `maxFiles=32` slice and prevented a later readable `src/main.js` from entering the bundle.

truth_boundaries: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. This prevents rejected context requests from starving valid later files; it does not guarantee that the resulting bounded context is semantically sufficient for arbitrary software goals.

`maxFiles` is now an accepted-file budget, while `maxBytes` remains a hard total-content budget; a later file that cannot fit the remaining byte budget is still skipped rather than forcing eviction or reordering.
Initial semantic seed priority across many otherwise admissible files remains a separate selection-quality question; this change preserves caller order rather than prescribing a new ranking policy.
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still lacks an atomic expected-base-SHA precondition, so external GET-to-PUT base races remain outside client-side elimination.
